messages:
Marta: quick heads-up — after last canary p99 jumped from ~180ms to ~540ms for a small subset of requests with long prompts + tool calls. p95 steady ~200ms.
Samir: thanks. I instrumented a few of the slow traces and saw kernel selector falling back to generic_attention on some sequences. flamegraph looks like generic_attn + extra kv work.
Jules: are those sequences hitting a different path (tool-call / external api) that changes token distribution?
Marta: yes — they include tool invocation tokens and a couple of regen steps on retries.
Samir: snippet from the profiler:
```
kernel_select:generic_attention 46%
kernel_select:fused_multi_head 28%
kv_cache:fetch_miss_recompute 18%
other:sys_overhead 8%
```
Samir: also saw microbatching behavior: microbatch_size=8, max_batch_hold_ms=20 in the canary. When generic_attn is chosen those requests block the batch longer and push others into tail.
Kevin: logs show kv_evictions spiking at same timestamps. evict_count per-session goes from ~2 -> 18 on those slow sessions. looks like regen triggers different session affinity so cache misses rewarm.
Jules: reconciling two things: (1) kernel fallback increases per-token CPU cost, (2) kv rewarm + recompile for mispredicted kernels multiplies latency.
Marta: tested reducing microbatch_size to 2 on a small pool — p99 dropped to ~260ms for these cases but throughput dropped ~22%. tradeoff obvious.
Samir: here's the command I used to repro locally:
```bash
RUNTIME_PROF=1 ./serve --microbatch 2 --max-hold-ms 10 --kernel-pin-threshold=1024
```
Samir: kernel-pin-threshold=1024 forces optimized kernel for sequences > 1024 tokens to avoid selector oscillation (we saw recompile churn).
Kevin: alternative is to detect tool-call markers and route them to a separate lane with different batching heuristics and longer kv retention.
Jules: on tool calls we also sometimes call external validators which can cause regen loops when response arrives late — that extends the end-to-end and invalidates KV assumptions.
Marta: agreed. proposed mitigation plan: 1) short-term: route requests with tool-call flag to dedicated low-concurrency lane with microbatch=2, pin kernel when seq_len > threshold, increase kv retention window (+30s) 2) medium: improve selector heuristics to avoid fallback if we know kv rewarm cost is high 3) long: add hedging for critical tail requests and better session-affinity keys for tool-invocations.
Samir: will run a quick sweep: microbatch [1,2,4,8], kv_retention [+0s,+30s,+60s], kernel_pin_threshold [512,1024,2048] and capture p95/p99 + throughput.
perf-bot: summary: canary 2146003200 -> p99 spike 180ms -> 540ms, correlated evict_count x9, kernel_fallback events +3x.
Marta: thanks. I'll spin up config change for routing tool-calls and run the sweep with Samir. if we see regression elsewhere we'll rollback.
Jules: also flagging product — tool authors should consider adding a non-blocking/async hook to avoid regen-on-sync patterns.
Kevin: +1. also adding a metric for kernel_selection_changes_per_request to alert earlier.
Marta: vote: quick experiment first, then selector tuning. any objections?
Samir: no objections.
Jules: :thumbsup:
perf-bot: note added to thread: experiment-id=exp-21460032-01
Marta: logging experiment as exp-21460032-01 and will post results here.
